title: Regular expression denial of service in email update via nested-quantifier regex
evidence: api_views/users.py:132 update_email reads JSON email; api_views/users.py:144 re.search with evil pattern on attacker string | validator: api_views/users.py:132 update_email reads attacker email from JSON body; api_views/users.py:144 re.search with nested-quantifier regex ^([0-9a-zA-Z]([-.\w]*[0-9a-zA-Z])@...) on unbounded str(request_data.get(email)) with no length/timeout guard | consensus: 1/1 confirmed | triage: Authenticated ReDoS in email regex with no length guard
rationale: PUT /users/v1/{username}/email passes attacker-controlled email directly to re.search with a vulnerable nested-quantifier pattern ([-.\w]* inside (...)* plus overlapping character classes). Crafted long emails cause catastrophic backtracking, blocking the worker (DoS). Cross-unit flow from authenticated request body to regex sink.
hunter_evidence: api_views/users.py:132 update_email reads JSON email; api_views/users.py:144 re.search with evil pattern on attacker string
patch_summary: Replace custom regex with simple validator or email-validator library, enforce max length and avoid nested quantifiers.

triage.rationale: Authenticated attacker controls email string into catastrophic nested-quantifier re.search causing CPU DoS
